purpose: Two new white male character templates with new generated bodies, distinct heads, compatible Mixamo animation and bounded structural controls.

operations.operation: Male A head P2 quad generation
Male B head P2 quad generation
Male A body P2 quad generation
Male B body P2 quad generation

historicalUncertainty: Period-informed fictional clothes based on dated collection examples; not a reconstruction of a particular person or occupation.
plan: Generate two new head bases and two new clothed bodies; no Samuel or player body reuse.
Use compatible Mixamo skeletons, verify weights and retarget nine body clips in Blender.
Fit eyes, lids, teeth, lips and expressions with measured anchors per head.
Add belly size, body width and restrained nose/ear/jaw/chin controls.
Provide hair and colour variation and compare both bases through motion.
Run source motion audits, screenshots, continuous closeups, gameplay paths and real-timer performance.

rejectedReviews.reason: Visible neck/collar gap, jagged donor boundary, layered eyelids and misplaced sideburns. Motion checks passed but the visible assembly failed.
User rejected visible wrist UV streaks, neck/collar fit, stiff workwear and eye appearance. Passing motion and browser checks did not establish visual quality.
Direct thigh skinning pulled the apron hem into separate flaps and left intermediate-pose intersections.
Simple leg bounds did not follow the actual trouser and waistband surfaces well enough.
The standing apron had an abrupt ledge below the shirt hem.
Removing the upright contact fit exposed trouser geometry through the apron.

fitTiming.scope: Isolated Character Lab, local Chrome, real browser timers; not whole-game FPS.

videoReview.scope: Recorded game entrance, turn and sit sequence; 12 sampled frames per template, plus consultation and examination PNGs.

repairs: Preserve the native throat, fit the neck inside the collar and bake skin onto unique UVs in 3D.
Keep facial structure rigid above a short neck blend and keep garment collar weights on the chest.
Remove disconnected hand-weighted cuff fragments; extend each native hand into the sleeve as a continuous weighted mesh.
Give the new wrist surface its own padded UV atlas and clean residual cuff pigment from the proximal hand.
Fit the apron to the final fused shirt, include the trouser waist in the seated collision fit and hide covered shirt buttons.
Use the same bounded body warp on garment layers and keep abdomen controls off the lower legs.
Adjust seated palm pitch to prevent isolated fingertips appearing through the apron.
Use actual thigh angle for the apron drape so the sit cue cannot fold it early while the patient is upright.
Fit the apron against two depth grids of the actual posed trousers and waist, with separate lap and knee-front contacts and matching shadows.
Remove the obsolete donor normal map from the new eyelids and reduce neutral aperture and sclera brightness.
Add a torso inspection view, a visible-surface picker and same-pose shadow diagnostics to the review tools.
Lower the head 12 mm and bound donor neck lean relative to the chest while preserving the head performance.
Preserve the native upper throat; replace the lower neck below a sloping under-jaw/nape cut and keep its final ring inside the collar.
Reduce shirt chest depth and sleeve volume, taper the waist and line the narrowed cuff openings.
Match hand and wrist texture colour to sampled cheek skin before applying the shared appearance palette.
Replace flat apron ribbons with thick webbing, reinforced tabs and a waist knot with hanging ties.
Add a rolled apron hem, separate tape textures and edge stitching; reduce the seated knee drop and shape the hem corners.
Fit the lower apron to the actual trouser waist and continue its standing surface smoothly below the shirt hem.
Start the seated drape from the whole curved waist and fade lap contact below the bib; interpolate neighbouring depth samples with conservative clearance.
limitations: The waist and lap folds still look too regular or stiff in some gestures. Further pattern, tension-fold and material work is needed; the experimental offline cloth bake was rejected.
The broad donor still shows poor formal hip and trouser seams in an unobstructed side view; these need a garment-level rebuild.
Procedural hair shows repeated fibre flow and needs a dedicated art pass.
Neutral eyelids and inner corners still look artificial at close range; donor ears and skin transitions remain rough.
The sofa blanket is smoother and double-sided but its source fold shape remains coarse.
Structural controls are bounded edits of two donors; arbitrary clothes are not interchangeable between bodies.
The apron uses a runtime vertex-shader fit; its source mesh alone does not include that correction, and CPU surface picks do not report the displaced contact point.
These replays verify the affected paths, not every combination of controls and motion. No whole-game performance claim is made.

experimentalClothBake.result: The local cloth tests did not produce usable folds. No simulated drape from those tests is included.

armReconstructionExperiment.direction: Evaluate a complete rigged worker asset and an established anatomical character generator instead of continuing procedural reconstruction.
armReconstructionExperiment.note: Intermediate assembled blends and the lean motion report are archived with the rejected reconstruction. The public assets and runtime have been restored to the previously verified garment pass.
